options: A read only copy that replays the primary's log, and is a little behind
A second primary that accepts writes
A backup file on disk
A cache that stores query results
why: It is read only, and it is a little behind.

q: A user saves a change, the page reloads from a replica, and the old value shows. What is this bug called?
options: A deadlock
A read-your-writes failure
A dirty write
A phantom read
why: A replica can be behind. A user may not see their own write there.

q: How can you fix that bug?
options: Add more replicas
Turn off replication
After a write, read from the primary, or wait until the replica has reached the write's LSN
Retry the page after 10 minutes
why: The LSN is the position in the log. When the replica has replayed it, the write is there.

q: How should you measure how far behind a replica is?
options: Look at the table size on the replica
Compare row counts every second
Use now() minus the last replay time on the replica
Use `replay_lag` on the primary, and do not alarm on now() minus the last replay time
why: now() minus the last replay time grows when nobody writes, even when the replica is fully caught up.

q: A long report query on a replica is cancelled with error 40001. What is the cause?
options: The replica must apply the primary's cleanup, and that conflicts with the long query. Retry, or give long reports their own replica
The replica ran out of disk
Reports are not allowed on replicas
The primary crashed
why: The replica applies the primary's cleanup.

q: What is the risk of asynchronous replication?
options: Writes become slower
If the primary dies, the last commits may be lost because the replica did not receive them yet
The replica can write data too
The primary stops accepting reads
why: Sync cannot lose commits, but writes wait for the replica, and they stop if the replica is gone.

q: During failover you promote a replica. What must you make sure of?
options: The old primary keeps running as normal
All replicas are turned off
The old primary can never accept writes again
The new primary has fewer connections
why: Two primaries that both accept writes split the data. Also check for replication slots nobody reads.
